answer: Each identity posts an 80-credit bond on a forecast, recorded on the pigment board, that it will deliver 8 jobs next epoch; receipts go to the ivory ledger, bound to one key, and cannot serve two identities. The k-th fake still posts a fresh 80, so cost grows linearly with no reuse; a short forecast burns 10 credits per missing job, so 1,000 fakes lock 80,000 credits and owe 8,000 distinct jobs, while an honest agent posts 80 once and keeps it by delivering 8. Forecast herding fails because shared receipts cluster, and a sable roll publishes burned forecasters for re-checking.
